🔴 As of February 21, 2026, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has signed decrees enacting National Security and Defense Council sanctions against 225 captains of the Russian "shadow fleet" for exporting oil in violation of international restrictions. 

These measures, which also target entities servicing the Russian military-industrial complex, align with ongoing efforts by the EU and G7 to curb Russia's ability to fund its war through oil revenue.

Zelensky signed two sanctions decrees aimed against Russia. Ukraine will share information with its partners to synchronize sanctions policy and plans to expand restrictions against individuals and entities that contribute to Russian aggression.

The list includes citizens of 11 countries, including Russia, India, and the Philippines. Monitoring of maritime traffic in the Black, Red, and Baltic Seas confirmed their involvement in operating vessels belonging to Russia’s so-called shadow fleet.

The second sanctions package covers 46 Russian nationals, two Iranian nationals, and 44 Russian companies servicing the country’s military-industrial complex.

Among them are the Plant of Control and Repair Laboratories (Engels), the Kazan Electrical Engineering Plant, the Kashin Electrical Equipment Plant, the Murom Radio Plant, the St. Petersburg Aircraft Repair Company, Tver Carriage Works, the Elektrotayga Plant in St. Petersburg, the Penza Precision Instrumentation Plant, the Zubovo-Polyansky Radio Parts Plant, the Ural Rubber Products Plant, the Kazan Radio Measuring Equipment Plant, as well as several design bureaus and research institutes.

According to Ukrainian authorities, these entities are involved in the supply, development, production, and repair of equipment, including electronic warfare systems and components used in the manufacture of ballistic and cruise missiles, attack and reconnaissance drones, small arms, and ammunition.

The two Iranian nationals were sanctioned for supplying aircraft parts and components in circumvention of international restrictions in the interests of the Iran Aircraft Manufacturing Industrial Company (HESA), which cooperates with Russia in the development and production of Shahed drones.
